title: How Many Seats Are Free Before This One?

concept.title: Keep a 0/1 array of free seats in a Fenwick tree and remember each seat's state to change it only when needed
body: A row of `n` seats starts empty. People take seats, leave them, and from time to time someone asks: **how many seats before the seat number `i` are free?** For 5 seats, after seats 2 and 4 are taken, the question about the seat 5 returns 2 (seats 1 and 3 are free among those before 5).

Let `free[s]` be 1 if the seat `s` is free and 0 if it is taken. The answer to a question is the sum `free[1] + ... + free[i-1]`, a prefix sum, so a Fenwick tree over `free` does the job. When a seat changes state, add the **change** to the tree: taking a free seat adds `-1`, freeing a taken seat adds `+1`. The operations that do not change anything (taking a taken seat, freeing a free seat) must not touch the tree, so keep the state of every seat in an array.

body.code:
state = [1] * (n + 1)                    # 1 = free
t = tree with 1 at every position
for kind, i in ops:
    if kind == 1 and state[i] == 1:        # take a free seat
        state[i] = 0; add(t, i, -1)
    elif kind == 2 and state[i] == 0:      # free a taken seat
        state[i] = 1; add(t, i, 1)
    elif kind == 3:
        print(prefix(t, i - 1))

body: Building the tree with a 1 at every position can be done by adding 1 `n` times (O(n log n)). Each operation takes O(log n). The check of the old state is what keeps the counts right when the same operation is repeated.

statement: `n` seats are all free at the start. Process `q` operations: type 1 `i` takes the seat `i`, type 2 `i` frees the seat `i` (repeating a state changes nothing), type 3 `i` asks how many free seats have a number smaller than `i`. Print the answers to the operations of type 3 on one line.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of seats and the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines has two numbers `t` and `i`. If `t = 1`, take the seat `i`; if `t = 2`, free the seat `i`; if `t = 3`, print how many seats with a number smaller than `i` are free.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 3, separated by spaces.
constraints: All seats are free at the start.
Taking a taken seat or freeing a free seat changes nothing.

examples.note: After taking the seats 2 and 4 the free seats before 5 are 1 and 3: 2. After freeing 2 the free seats before 3 are 1 and 2: 2.

hints: Treat the seats as a 0/1 array and sum its prefix.
Add -1 when a free seat is taken and +1 when a taken seat is freed.
Keep the state of every seat to ignore repeated operations.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

# Your code here

explanation: The free seats form a 0/1 array in a Fenwick tree; a change of state adds -1 or +1 only when the state really changes, and a question is a prefix sum.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).
